title: On the structure of countable hyperspaces of regular subcontinua
description:
Let X be a metric continuum and let D(X) be its hyperspace of regular subcontinua, that is, of the subcontinua of X which are the closure of their interior. We prove that if D(X) is countable, then the interiors of its minimal elements are dense in X, and every regular subcontinuum is determined by the minimal elements it contains. We further establish that D(X) is a Gδ subset of the hyperspace C(X) of subcontinua whenever X admits a family of regular subcontinua whose interiors have dense union and which satisfies an absorption property. Consequently, every countable D(X) is completely metrizable and scattered. In particular, D(X) is never homeomorphic to the rational numbers, which answers a question of Ramírez Angarita and of Camargo, Ordoñez and Ramírez. The theorems of the paper are formalized in Lean 4.

Lean formalization. Every numbered theorem, lemma, proposition and corollary of Sections 1 and 3–6, and Proposition 7.5, is proved in Lean 4 (v4.35.0-rc2) with Mathlib, using only Lean's standard axioms; the examples and remarks are not formalized. Lean Comparator accepted the solution in a sandbox (Lean kernel, nanoda, con-ron).

Also available as aiXiv:2611.01165 (https://aixiv.online/abs/2611.01165).
